opacity.plain: an area that looks different from the surrounding tissue
opacity.context: Opacity describes an appearance on an image; it is not a diagnosis by itself.

nodule.context: A nodule is a description of shape and size. Its meaning depends on location, history, and comparison imaging.

lesion.plain: an area of tissue that appears different
lesion.context: Lesion is a broad descriptive term and does not by itself say whether a change is harmful.

mass.plain: an area or lump seen on the study
mass.context: Mass describes a finding. Additional clinical context is needed to determine its cause.

effusion.context: An effusion means fluid is present in a space where the report is looking.

fracture.plain: a break or crack in a bone
fracture.context: The report wording and clinical examination determine the type and significance of a fracture.

consolidation.plain: an area of lung filled with material instead of air
consolidation.context: Consolidation is an imaging pattern with several possible causes; the report and clinician provide context.

cardiomegaly.context: This describes heart size on the image and can be affected by imaging technique.

hypoechoic.plain: an area that appears darker on ultrasound
hypoechoic.context: Hypoechoic describes appearance, not a specific diagnosis.

osteolytic.plain: an area where bone appears to have been broken down
osteolytic.context: This is an imaging description that needs clinical evaluation to determine the cause.

fundus.plain: the interior back surface of the eye
fundus.context: Examining the fundus allows a clinician to see the retina, optic disc, and blood vessels directly.

retina.plain: the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye
retina.context: The retina acts like camera film, sending visual images to the brain.

macula.plain: the central part of the retina used for sharp, detailed vision
macula.context: The macula is responsible for clear central vision needed for reading and recognizing faces.

fovea.plain: the very center point of the retina responsible for the sharpest vision
fovea.context: The fovea provides high-resolution color and detail vision.

microaneurysm.plain: a tiny bulge in a retinal blood vessel
microaneurysm.context: Microaneurysms are small balloon-like outpouchings in blood vessels, often the earliest visible sign of diabetic retinopathy.

microaneurysms.plain: tiny bulges in retinal blood vessels
microaneurysms.context: Microaneurysms are small outpouchings in blood vessels, often the earliest visible sign of diabetic eye changes.

exudate.plain: a deposit of fluid, fat, or protein that leaked from blood vessels
exudate.context: Exudates are seen when blood vessel walls become leaky or permeable.

exudates.plain: deposits of fat and protein that leaked from blood vessels
exudates.context: Hard exudates appear as yellow spots in the retina where damaged vessels have leaked fluid.

hard exudates.plain: yellowish lipid and protein deposits on the retina
hard exudates.context: Hard exudates indicate chronic leakage from compromised retinal capillaries.

cotton wool spot.plain: a fluffy white patch on the retina caused by reduced blood flow
cotton wool spot.context: Cotton wool spots represent localized swelling of nerve fibers where micro-circulation was disrupted.

cotton wool spots.plain: fluffy white patches on the retina caused by reduced blood flow
cotton wool spots.context: Cotton wool spots indicate areas where small retinal blood vessels have temporarily closed.

hemorrhage.plain: an area of bleeding or escaped blood
hemorrhage.context: Retinal hemorrhages occur when weakened capillaries leak blood into the retinal layers.

hemorrhages.plain: areas of bleeding or escaped blood
hemorrhages.context: Retinal hemorrhages occur when weakened capillaries leak blood into the retinal layers.

dot and blot hemorrhages.plain: small round spots of bleeding in the deeper retina
dot and blot hemorrhages.context: Dot and blot hemorrhages are typical signs of retinal blood vessel damage from diabetes.

neovascularization.plain: the growth of abnormal, fragile new blood vessels
neovascularization.context: In advanced diabetic retinopathy, the eye grows fragile new vessels that easily bleed and cause vision complications.

macular edema.plain: swelling and fluid buildup in the center of the retina
macular edema.context: Macular edema occurs when leaking blood vessels cause the central retina to swell, potentially blurring vision.

drusen.plain: small yellow fatty deposits beneath the retina
drusen.context: Drusen are tiny deposits of waste products that accumulate under the retinal pigment layer.

papilledema.plain: swelling of the optic nerve head
papilledema.context: Papilledema usually reflects elevated pressure inside the skull and requires urgent medical evaluation.

vitreous hemorrhage.plain: bleeding into the clear gel that fills the inside of the eye
vitreous hemorrhage.context: A vitreous hemorrhage can suddenly block vision and needs prompt ophthalmologist assessment.

tractional retinal detachment.plain: pulling and separation of the retina caused by scar tissue
tractional retinal detachment.context: Fibrous scar tissue from abnormal blood vessels can pull the retina away from the back wall of the eye.

diabetic retinopathy.plain: changes in retinal blood vessels caused by diabetes
diabetic retinopathy.context: Diabetic retinopathy is a complication of diabetes where high blood sugar weakens retinal blood vessels.
